title: Derived geometric stalk of a constant local model
statement: Let $f:U\to X$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] and $A$ a commutative ring. Use the small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], their constant-$A$ module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], and the derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $K\in D(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and let $E^\bullet$ be a cochain complex of $A$-modules; write $\underline{E^\bullet}_U$ for its termwise constant sheaf complex [def-kun-constant-sheaf]. Suppose an isomorphism $\alpha:f^{-1}K\xrightarrow{\sim}\underline{E^\bullet}_U$ is given, where $f^{-1}$ is the exact constant-coefficient module inverse image [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. For every geometric point $\bar u:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to U$, with $\Omega$ algebraically closed [def-weil-geometric-point], put $\bar x=f\circ\bar u$. Applying the exact stalk functor termwise to representatives of $\alpha$ gives an $A$-linear isomorphism $K_{\bar x}\xrightarrow{\sim}E^\bullet$ in $D(A)$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. Here $K_{\bar x}$ is the derived object obtained by termwise geometric stalks; its coefficient ring is identified with $A$ by the constant-section stalk map. No boundedness, finiteness, constructibility or Tor-amplitude hypothesis is imposed.
